summary:
The bullpen category is the story across the board today — R1, R2, and R3 all carry 3-game win streaks on bullpen with a matching 54% mark over the last 14 days (102-88, n=190) versus season baselines in the 51-52% range, a clean +2-3pt jump on a workable sample. Meanwhile SP rating is ice cold for R3 specifically (47%, -5.0pts flagged), and it's shaky across R1/R2 too at 46% over the last 14. That split matters today because several of the top-delta games are pitching-driven matchups where the model still leans hard on the bullpen side of its math — MIL's +2.53 CONSENSUS over SEA lines up with a team the model already loves (MIL picks going 25-15, 62%, and +4.0u when strong-play flagged), and Robert Gasser walking into Milwaukee's bullpen-favored profile makes this the highest-confidence board play. CLE's smaller but unanimous CLE lean (+0.61 to +1.26) versus SFG is another spot where trends+bullpen alignment should carry more weight than the SP number given today's cold SP signal.

STL @ CIN is the largest gap on the slate at a full CONSENSUS -2.27 for STL across all four ratings, but treat it cautiously — R3 carries the worst recent strong-play stretch (14d: 41-46, 47%, -5.0u) and its SP cold streak, so lean on trends+runs (55.7% season, the best combo on the board) rather than the SP séance in shaping conviction here. TBR's leaning CONSENSUS for TOR @ TBR is worth a second look too: TBR-picked games hit 71% (25-10) on the year with a strong +22.0u mark, one of the best team-when-liked profiles in the sample, and today's delta trend (+0.35 to +1.08) is climbing across ratings, suggesting the room's already lining up with TBR before puck-drop numbers finalize. Skip or shade HOU despite the R4 mild lean (+0.52) — HOU strong-play record is ugly at 3-8 (27%, -8.0u), the weakest team profile in the book, and LAA @ HOU's marginal deltas (+0.09 to +0.52) aren't enough signal to override that red flag.
